name: Bifrost Python CodeQL quality
description: Public Python structural and quality policies aligned with reviewed CodeQL query identities and engine fact contracts.

policies.severity_rationale: An inconsistent C3 linearization makes Python class creation fail with TypeError, preventing the class and dependent imports from loading.
policies.remediation: Reorder or redesign the direct base classes so Python can construct a consistent method resolution order.

policies.severity_rationale: A class that defines hashing without its own equality implementation can violate the equality and hash contract expected by dictionaries and sets.
policies.remediation: Implement a compatible __eq__ method or remove the custom __hash__ method; inherited equality does not replace a direct implementation.

policies.severity_rationale: An explicit super() class argument that differs from the enclosing class starts lookup at the wrong point in the MRO and can break cooperative method calls.
policies.remediation: Pass the enclosing class as super()'s first argument, or use zero-argument super() where appropriate.

policies.severity_rationale: A superclass initializer's proven attribute write can hide a descendant method and break method dispatch; a read-only property can additionally make initialization fail.
policies.remediation: Rename the initializer field or descendant method, or provide a compatible writable property when the assignment is intentional.

policies.severity_rationale: An unresolved or non-class base is a definite inference failure. Runs report inconclusive when inference fails so hierarchy-dependent checks retain their uncertainty.
policies.remediation: Correct the base expression so it resolves to a class, or make the intended base class available to analysis.

policies.severity_rationale: A mutation of a mutable parameter default persists across calls and can make function behavior depend on call order.
policies.remediation: Copy or create a fresh mutable value inside the function, or avoid mutating the default.

policies.severity_rationale: The site module convenience functions may be unavailable when Python starts with -S.
policies.remediation: Use an explicit status return or raise SystemExit at the command-line boundary.

policies.severity_rationale: A global declaration at module scope has no effect on name binding.
policies.remediation: Remove the redundant module-scope global declaration.

policies.severity_rationale: An unread module-level value is likely dead state and can mislead readers about which bindings affect behavior.
policies.remediation: Remove the unused binding or add the intended use.

policies.severity_rationale: A public, stateless class with no more than one public method adds indirection without providing a meaningful class role.
policies.remediation: Replace the class with a function or simple value when that preserves its API and behavior.

policies.severity_rationale: Complex destructor control flow is difficult to reason about and runs during object finalization.
policies.remediation: Simplify __del__; move cleanup into an explicit, idempotent method or context manager.

policies.severity_rationale: Using both import forms for one local module in the same scope makes names and dependencies harder to follow.
policies.remediation: Choose either module-qualified imports or selected from-imports consistently.

policies.severity_rationale: Importing the current module through its own name is redundant and can expose partially initialized state.
policies.remediation: Remove the self-import and refer to local declarations directly.

policies.severity_rationale: A wildcard import without an explicit export list injects an uncontrolled set of names into the importing scope.
policies.remediation: Import the required names explicitly or define a deliberate __all__ export list.

policies.severity_rationale: Python syntax errors prevent execution and make analysis of the affected code unreliable.
policies.remediation: Correct the parser-reported syntax error before relying on analysis or running the module.

policies.severity_rationale: A module can read a cyclically imported member before the target module executes its definition, causing import-time failure.
policies.remediation: Break the import cycle or move the member use until after both modules finish initialization.

policies.severity_rationale: Reading a local variable on a path before it is initialized can raise an exception at runtime.
policies.remediation: Initialize the variable on every path before the read, or restructure the conditional logic.

policies.severity_rationale: A comparison between constant expressions has a fixed result and can leave a mistaken or dead condition.
policies.remediation: Replace it with the intended boolean constant or compare the intended runtime values.

policies.severity_rationale: Identity comparison can disagree with value equality for operands whose supported classes define value equality.
policies.remediation: Use == or != for value comparisons and retain is for singleton checks.

policies.severity_rationale: Identity of small integers and short strings may depend on CPython interning behavior.
policies.remediation: Compare the values with == or != rather than relying on object interning.

policies.severity_rationale: A later equal dictionary key overwrites the earlier value, which can silently discard data.
policies.remediation: Remove or rename the repeated key and keep the intended value.

policies.severity_rationale: Named percent conversions require mapping keys; a non-mapping operand raises a runtime TypeError.
policies.remediation: Supply a mapping containing each named format key.

policies.severity_rationale: A conversion count that differs from the known positional operand count raises a runtime formatting error.
policies.remediation: Make the conversion and supplied value counts agree.

policies.severity_rationale: == may invoke value equality and does not express the intended None singleton test.
policies.remediation: Use is None or is not None for singleton checks.

policies.severity_rationale: A missing positional format value raises an exception when str.format is evaluated.
policies.remediation: Supply enough positional values for the highest numeric field.

policies.severity_rationale: A named field without a matching keyword raises an exception when str.format is evaluated.
policies.remediation: Supply the required keyword or change the format field.

policies.severity_rationale: Legacy leading-zero octal notation is easy to misread and is rejected by modern Python syntax.
policies.remediation: Write octal literals with the explicit 0o prefix.

policies.severity_rationale: A proven unused positional value often indicates a format call that does not match its template.
policies.remediation: Remove the extra positional value or add the corresponding field.

policies.severity_rationale: A proven unused keyword indicates a mismatch between the format template and its arguments.
policies.remediation: Remove the unused keyword or add a matching named field.

policies.severity_rationale: A tuple is truthy when it is nonempty, so asserting it does not validate its elements.
policies.remediation: Assert the intended condition or validate the tuple contents explicitly.

policies.severity_rationale: A class with finalizer cleanup and neither context-manager method can make deterministic resource release difficult.
policies.remediation: Implement both __enter__ and __exit__, or use a resource abstraction that provides deterministic cleanup.

policies.severity_rationale: Mixing value returns with reachable implicit None returns gives callers inconsistent result behavior.
policies.remediation: Return an explicit value on every reachable path, or make the callable consistently return None.

policies.severity_rationale: Different tuple lengths across return paths make callers handle an inconsistent result shape.
policies.remediation: Return tuples with a consistent arity or use a named result type for varying data.

policies.severity_rationale: Raising outside a special method's protocol can replace the expected exception and make normal operations fail unexpectedly.
policies.remediation: Raise an exception allowed by the special-method contract, or handle the underlying failure locally.
